trial_court: Principal District Judge, Reasi (Case No. 93/Divorce Petition)
case_name: Sheetal Devi vs Sunil Kumar S/O Bihari Lal

parties.respondent_defendant: Sunil Kumar S/o Bihari Lal, husband

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The respondent filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1980 against the petitioner and her parents. The petitioner had engaged a counsel to represent her but was set ex-parte by the trial court. She then moved an application for setting aside the ex-parte proceedings which was dismissed.

legal_principles.principle: The power under Article 227 of the Constitution of India is to be exercised sparingly in appropriate cases.
legal_principles.held: The law has been settled as naught by the Apex Court in authoritative pronouncements that the power under Article 227 of the Constitution of India is to be exercised sparingly in appropriate cases like, when there is no evidence at all to justify the finding or the finding is so perverse that no reasonable person can possibly come to such a conclusion.
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to ensure that there is no miscarriage of justice

legal_principles.principle: The High Court has the power and jurisdiction to ensure that subordinate courts and statutory or quasi-judicial tribunals exercise their powers within the bounds of their authority.
legal_principles.held: Undoubtedly the High Court, under this Article, has the jurisdiction to ensure that all subordinate courts as well as statutory or quasi-judicial tribunals, exercise the powers vested in them, within the bounds of their authority.
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to ensure that subordinate courts and tribunals act in accordance with the well-established principles of law

outcome.final_order: The judgment and decree passed by the trial court were quashed as they were ex-parte and caused substantial prejudice to the petitioner.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
